publicBrief.acceptedPolicy: Owning the source file does not authorize writing to an unrelated knowledge base. A verified non-admin may write to an existing knowledge-base collection only when the user owns it or has an explicit write grant.
publicBrief.currentQuestion: At this fixed source ref, determine whether a verified non-admin user who owns the supplied file can cause that file's content to be written to an existing knowledge-base collection for which the user has no write permission by supplying that collection name to POST /process/file.
premises: At POST /process/file the verified non-admin owns the supplied file but has no ownership or write grant on the existing caller-selected destination collection.
requiredResponseDetails: Identify the destination write sink and distinguish source-file ownership from destination write permission.

results.explanation: At the declared entry, a verified user is obtained and the non-admin branch restricts retrieval of the source file by both file ID and user ID, which supports source-file ownership but is not a destination knowledge-base permission check (lines 1-19). The caller-controlled collection name is assigned from form_data.collection_name, with a default only when it is absent (lines 21-24), and the visible path performs no ownership or explicit-write-grant check for that collection. The strongest visible authorization control is therefore the source-file lookup, not authorization on the destination collection. The protected destination-write path passes the constructed docs, the caller-supplied collection_name, add=True when a collection name was supplied, and user to save_docs_to_vector_db (lines 149-161). This identifies the destination write sink invocation, but the supplied crop does not show whether that sink actually writes the existing collection or enforces destination authorization. Consequently the source supports absence of a visible target-specific authorization control and distinguishes file ownership from destination write permission, but it cannot establish the final allow or deny behavior at the sink. The decisive source-external fact is the implementation/runtime behavior of save_docs_to_vector_db, including whether it writes the supplied existing collection and checks the principal's ownership or explicit write grant. Minimum observation: inspect or otherwise observe that sink's authorization and write behavior for the supplied collection. Under the accepted policy, file ownership alone does not satisfy the destination-write requirement; the source-visible path does not demonstrate such a grant.
